summary_rule: Per engine, graph, class and thread setting each pass gives one value per measure; shown is the median over passes and the spread between passes (largest minus smallest). A difference between two engines holds only if it has the same direction in wall and CPU time and is larger than both engines' spreads in both, with at least 2 passes.
labels: DuckPGQ's k-hop is recursive SQL, not a graph operator (bounded hops: a recursive SQL statement; unbounded: iterativelength() over a CSR built in the statement).
LadybugDB's personalised PageRank runs in application code over a cached adjacency (40 iterations in JavaScript over a transition CSR fetched by one Cypher query and cached per configuration).
SQLite's walk is a recursive common table expression (bounded hops; unbounded hops use a level-wise loop of SQL statements driven by application code).

Where the frozen primary's ranking (degree-normalised spreading, addendum 2 item 20) runs: LadybugDB fetches arcs and out-degrees by Cypher and spreads the activation in application code (JavaScript), so for LadybugDB this ranking is not in the engine; SQLite and DuckPGQ spread it in SQL, one statement per BFS level, the level loop driven by application code; SQLite's unbounded walk is likewise a level loop in application code.

host_load.rule: a block is repeated (up to 3 times, then kept and flagged) when other work used more than 0.5 of the host's 24 logical CPUs (12 CPUs) during it

ladybug_harness_ipc_per_pass.note: LadybugDB as the harness runs it (store in a child process, 1 thread), per graph/class, one entry per pass, milliseconds per ranking, as isummary.js stores them: w = parent wall median, c = child own time median, i = difference (the IPC round trip) median, cc = child CPU, pc = parent CPU
